Author: Troy Nelson
Source Summary: The book is organized as a 52-week program with 365 exercises, one lick per day, designed to develop, improve, and maintain guitar technique.
Hearth Application: This is a strong source model for the Practice node: daily contact, small repeatable challenge, long arc, visible streak, and rotation through technique categories.
Notes: The printed page mapping is rough because early front matter/page numbering is inconsistent.

Author: Troy Nelson
Source Summary: The introduction rejects bland chromatic exercise books and aims for technique examples that apply to real musical settings across styles such as rock, blues, jazz, country, and funk.
Hearth Application: The Hearth Practice node should avoid sterile drills. Even technical exercises should feel connected to musical use, style, sound, and future expression.
Notes: Central design principle for drill authoring.

Author: Troy Nelson
Source Summary: The introduction names monotony as a problem in practice and presents fun, musically relevant material as part of the solution.
Hearth Application: Practice design should protect motivation. A learner returns when the drill feels like a small musical spell, not punishment.
Notes: Useful for tone of Practice node.

Author: Troy Nelson
Source Summary: The book rotates seven techniques, one for each day of the week: alternate picking, string skipping, string bending, arpeggios, sweep picking, legato, and rhythm.
Hearth Application: The Practice node can use rotating daily categories. This creates variety while keeping a stable ritual: each day has a technical focus.

Author: Troy Nelson
Source Summary: Alternate picking is presented as a fundamental technique that can be applied in any musical context.
Hearth Application: Doing/Practice should treat alternate picking as early core technique: not flashy, but the hand's basic engine for many later skills.

Author: Troy Nelson
Source Summary: String skipping is framed as useful beyond rock/metal, with examples in blues, jazz, rock, and metal.
Hearth Application: String skipping can become a later coordination challenge: the player learns to cross space deliberately rather than only moving stepwise.

Author: Troy Nelson
Source Summary: String bending examples include quarter-step, half-step, whole-step, oblique, unison, compound, and pre-bends.
Hearth Application: Bending belongs where technique starts becoming voice. Teach it as pitch control and emotional inflection, not just finger strength.
Notes: Connects to improvisation and blues expression.

Author: Troy Nelson
Source Summary: The book notes that an arpeggio is not itself a technique, but the coordinated right- and left-hand movement required to perform one qualifies as technical practice.
Hearth Application: Good distinction for Knowing/Doing: arpeggios are harmony unfolded, but practicing them trains coordination and map awareness.
Notes: Pairs with Dummies arpeggio source notes.

Author: Troy Nelson
Source Summary: Exercises are placed in musical style contexts such as rock, blues, jazz, metal, country, and funk.
Hearth Application: Practice challenges should include style tags. A lick is easier to care about when the learner knows what musical world it belongs to.

Author: Troy Nelson
Source Summary: The CD track listings include rhythm tracks at different BPMs and styles, supporting practice across tempos.
Hearth Application: Practice sessions should store BPM, tempo range, and pass condition. The app can encourage slow-to-clean before speed.
Notes: Exact tempo data can be extracted later if needed.

Author: Troy Nelson
Concept: Week 1 as pattern of rotating challenge
Source Summary: Week 1 introduces daily exercises across multiple techniques, each with a music description, technique, genre, tip, and tempo marking.
Hearth Application: This suggests a useful drill object shape: title, technique, genre/style, description, physical tip, tempo range, source reference, and pass condition.

Author: Troy Nelson
Source Summary: Each exercise includes a short tip, often about picking direction, fretting-hand preparation, bend intonation, or not rushing rhythmic figures.
Hearth Application: The app should store micro-corrections with drills. These become the guide's voice during practice: one precise thing to notice.
